name: Borrowed Stillness

detectability.signature: An absence rather than a presence: cosmic background radiation drops to zero across the sphere, and gravimetric readings flatline completely

proximity: Sensor noise fades eerily as ambient radiation begins to thin
Starlight dims perceptibly even though no object occludes it
contact: All external signals cease; vessels hear only their own life support
Momentum feels subtly wrong, as if inertia were being politely withheld
prolonged_exposure: Crew report deep psychological calm bordering on reluctance to leave
Atomic clocks aboard fall out of agreement with outside references by microseconds per day

phenomena: Visible distortion where the starfield flattens into muted grays at the boundary
Total absence of background radiation within, a silence measurable by any instrument
Objects entering appear slightly smaller than their true size to outside observers
hazards: Disorientation from total sensory deprivation during extended transit
Chronic clock drift complicating precision navigation fixes afterward
opportunities: Hidden base location; the pocket defeats passive detection entirely
Unique research opportunity to study a region apparently excised from normal spacetime
Emergency escape route, as pursuit rarely follows into absolute sensory silence
known_incidents: The survey drone Kestrel-9 drifted inside for three years before retrieval; its recordings contained thirty seconds of audio that matched nothing mechanical aboard
At least two pirate syndicates have historically used the pocket as a staging vault, judging by salvage tags recovered at its center
description: Borrowed Stillness is a sphere of nothing thirty thousand kilometers wide: not vacuum, which hums with background radiation, but a genuine absence where the cosmic murmur simply stops. To the eye it is a subtle flattening of stars, a patch of sky gone quietly gray. Instruments find it only by what is missing.

It has not moved, pulsed, or changed in any way since detection, and crossings are uneventful in the extreme. Inside, ships coast in perfect quiet, their hulls ticking in the sudden silence, and momentum behaves with a strange courtesy that pilots describe as being carried rather than coasting. Nothing has ever been harmed by entering; several crews have reported being reluctant to leave.

The retrieval of drone Kestrel-9, after three uneventful years adrift at the pocket's heart, remains its defining incident, along with thirty seconds of unexplained audio in the drone's final log. Pirate syndicates have valued its total radar silence for generations, and at least one cache of stolen freight is believed to rest permanently at its center. Physicists classify it as a region subtracted from spacetime, and decline to speculate further.

No warning beacons mark it because none seem necessary; the greatest danger it poses is a lingering fondness for its silence. Research foundations petition annually for exclusive study rights and are annually refused. For travelers, it remains a curiosity: a place where the universe holds its breath, and where nothing, so far, has ever gone wrong.
